title: Keep loyalty points right when long histories run in parallel

blocks.text: The shop's loyalty service has always been right for ordinary members. Since histories of a thousand entries or more started running on a parallel stream, the long-standing members complain: one sees thousands of points she never earned, another a balance that has nothing to do with what he redeemed.
`LoyaltyPoints` picks the stream for you. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/LoyaltyPoints.java`:

items: `earned(...)`: the welcome bonus, given once, plus the points of every purchase;
`remaining(...)`: the opening balance less every redemption.

blocks.text: Each must give the same answer whether the stream it gets is sequential or parallel. About two lines in total.

cases.says: for short histories, the points are the bonus plus every purchase, and the balance is the opening less every redemption
a history long enough to run in parallel still counts the welcome bonus exactly once
a long history of redemptions run in parallel leaves the opening balance less their sum

origin.section: reduce Needs an Identity That Changes Nothing and an Operation That Can Be Regrouped

concepts: reduce's identity must leave every element unchanged, because a parallel stream starts every chunk from it; a value such as a fee used as identity is added once per chunk.
reduce's operation must be associative; a running subtraction gives the right answer sequentially and a different one in parallel.
